title: Design release 1 gives a trader a saved address book they can search, filter by type, add to, view, edit and delete; Frontend has no address-book page and its journey can only read the book

finding.frontend: Frontend has no address book as a page. Its service navigation carries no items, so nothing links to a saved-addresses page, and searching the rendered DOM of all 31 captured Frontend screens and 36 captured states for "address book" or "add a new address" returns nothing. A trader meets the organisation's book only inside the five consignment party pickers and the contact-address page, and there only as a read-only chooser: the pickers offer a Search input hinted "Name, address or country", a secondary Search button, a five-row results table with a radio per row and a "View details" expander, pagination, and "Save and continue" (src/server/app/sets/live-animals/journeys/linear/features/addresses/party-picker/_address-picker.njk:69-113), and the contact-address page offers the whole book as one radio list. Nothing anywhere adds, changes or removes a record. Frontend's address-book service exposes only search, all and party, and states the split as a design decision: "This service reads and never writes. The notification journey selects from the organisation's book; adding, changing and removing the records in it belongs to the INS frontend, which is the only writer" (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). Frontend's records also carry no address type at all, deliberately, because the same record may be a consignor on one notification and a consignee on the next (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-15).
finding.prototype: Design release 1 gives the trader an address book of their own, reached from a service-navigation item on every page, and eight captured screens describe it. dr1-address-book is the list: heading "Address book", intro "Manage your addresses for use across import notifications.", a primary "Add a new address" button, a "Filter addresses" panel holding a Search box placeholdered "Search by name, address or country" and a "Type" select offering Place of Origin, Consignor, Consignee, Importer, Place of Destination, Transporter and Branch Address, a result count ("Showing 1-8 of 58"), a Name / Type / Address / Country table with a "View" link per row, and pagination (app/views/address-book.html:34-45). dr1-address-book-add is the type chooser: "What is the new address for?", one addressType radio group over those same seven types, each with its own hint, and a Continue button. dr1-address-book-lookup is the add form: "Add address details", a "Search for an address" type-ahead writing a hidden addressBookLookupAddressId, an "Enter address manually" toggle, "Save and continue" and "Cancel and return to address book". dr1-address-book-lookup-results is that page with the type-ahead panel open over candidate addresses. dr1-address-book-lookup-manual is that page with the manual reveal open, showing nine fields under two headings: Address (Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, County (optional), Postcode or Zip code, Country) and Contact details (Email address, Phone number, hinted "For international numbers include the country code"). dr1-address-book-add-from-party-picker is the same add form entered from a consignment party picker, with the type chooser skipped because the section implies the type and its answer carried in a hidden addressType. dr1-address-book-view is one saved address, headed with its own name, presented as a summary list of eight of those nine facts — County (optional) is not shown — with an "Edit" button and a red "Delete" button. dr1-address-book-edit is "Edit address and contact details": all nine fields, prefilled and already open, the search hidden, "Save changes" and "Cancel". So Design release 1's book is create, read, update and delete, and every saved address carries a type.
finding.difference: This is the one scope question in this comparison that a person has to settle, and it is stated here rather than decided. Two previous runs dropped these screens without photographing them; this run photographed all eight and they are enumerated above. The evidence for OUT of scope is strong, and it is not the reasoning either previous run used: the Import Notification Service front door, trade-imports-ins-frontend, already implements this address book at Design release 1's own URLs — /address-book, /address-book/add, /address-book/{id}, /address-book/{id}/edit and /address-book/{id}/delete — and its add form carries exactly the nine field labels above in Design release 1's wording, down to the phone hint; the address-book service behind it already serves create, update and delete; and this frontend's own service says writing belongs to that other service (src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:17-19). The evidence for IN scope is that Design release 1 puts the book behind a service-navigation item on the same service as the notification journey (app/views/layouts/main.html:16) and routes into it from inside a notification (app/routes.js:3598-3600), so to a user it is one service and not two. What settles it is one thing a person can state: whether the trade-imports-ins-frontend address book is the address book Design release 1 describes. It is not yet the same book in one respect that the person deciding should know about: Design release 1 types every saved address and offers a Type filter over seven types, while the INS front door's add form asks for no type, its list has no Type column, and the address book API's locked wire contract (OperatorResponse in trade-imports-address-book) carries no type or role field — so whichever service owns these pages, the seven address types are unbuilt everywhere. If the INS book is Design release 1's book, this finding is struck and the work left in this repo is the route out of a party picker, raised separately as address-book--no-route-to-add-an-address-from-a-picker because it stands whichever way this goes, and the address types, raised separately as address-book--picker-lists-every-saved-address-regardless-of-role because they bite inside the notification journey today. If it is not, this becomes one add-page piece of work covering all eight screens above, plus a write path in Frontend's address-book service. controls is deliberately empty: the finding is that eight whole pages have no counterpart, and cropping any single control on them would show less than the page does.
finding.falsifiedBy: Finding a route in trade-imports-animals-frontend that renders a saved-address list, add, view, edit or delete page. Searching src/server for "address-book" returns the read-only service, its client and its callers, and no registered path beginning /address-book.
finding.verification: Ran the falsifier: grepped the rendered DOM of all 67 captured Frontend files for "address book", "add a new address", "add an address" and "address-book" — nothing on either pattern set, so the absence holds. Opened dr1-address-book.png, dr1-address-book-view.png and dr1-address-book-lookup-results.png and read the rendered DOM of all eight prototype screens; every list-page element the author names is in dr1-address-book.html (heading, intro, primary button, Filter addresses panel, the search placeholder, the seven Type options, "Showing 1-8 of 58") and the filter panel is open in the picture, not collapsed. Checked the seven addressType radio values on dr1-address-book-add.html, the nine manual labels and both section headings on dr1-address-book-lookup-manual.html, and the nine prefilled labels plus "Save changes"/"Cancel" on dr1-address-book-edit.html. Checked the DR1 citations are root views and land on what the sentence says: app/views/address-book.html:34-45 is the heading, intro and add button. Checked the frontend citations verbatim at src/server/app/services/address-book/index.js:12-19 and confirmed the module exports only search, all and party. Verified the INS claim in the other repo: the five paths exist in src/server/address-book/{list,add,view,edit,delete}/index.js and src/server/address-book/add/index.njk:26-104 carries the nine labels and the phone hint in Design release 1's wording. Rubric 2 fired on one sentence — see correction. Band left at disputed: the open question here is whether the finding is about the right application, which is the disputed band's first meaning, not a desirability question.
finding.correction: Two changes. (1) The author wrote that dr1-address-book-view presents "those same nine facts". It presents eight: dr1-address-book-view.html has exactly eight govuk-summary-list__key rows — Name or organisation name, Address line 1, Address line 2 (optional), Town or city, Postcode or Zip code, Country, Email address, Phone number — and County (optional) is absent, which the screenshot confirms. The prototype slot now says eight of the nine, and says "all nine" of the edit page, where all nine labels are present (dr1-address-book-edit.html carries address-book-manual-county). (2) The difference slot's settling question is unchanged, but one true fact bearing directly on it was missing and has been added: the INS front door implements Design release 1's URLs and field labels but not its type model — its add form asks no address type, its list has no Type column, and the address-book API's wire contract carries no type or role field. Everything else the author claimed was checked and stands, including the eight-screen enumeration, the INS URL set, the INS field labels, and the read-only service comment quoted verbatim.

relatedTo.why: That finding names where the missing address book bites a user mid-journey, and it is the part of this one that survives even if the eight pages are ruled out of scope.

The seven address types this finding enumerates are the same types the pickers filter on; that finding is the part of the type model that bites inside the notification journey whichever service owns these eight pages.
